notes: technology_class 'gaseous_tpc' is used as the closest available enum value; NEWS-G's spherical proportional counter is not a true time-projection chamber (no drift+readout planes, single central sensor electrode instead). The ontology has no dedicated SPC class.

placements.note: Relationship to the SNOLAB S140 sphere (same unit temporarily relocated, or a second sphere) is not established by any source fetched this session.
placements.quote: New results from a 10 day physics run with a 135 cm in diameter spherical proportional counter at the Laboratoire Souterrain de Modane are reported.

sphere_diameter_s140.quote: 135 cm in diameter" spherical copper vessel

summary.plain: A hollow copper sphere filled with gas and a tiny sensor at its centre, sensitive enough to notice a single electron freed when a particle bumps a gas atom.
summary.technical: Spherical proportional counter: 60 cm SEDINE sphere (Ne+CH4, 3.1 bar) operated at LSM through 2015; 135 cm 'S140' copper sphere (pure CH4, 135 mbar) installed at SNOLAB 2020-2021, operating since summer 2021; a 135 cm sphere also ran a 10-day methane run at LSM reported in 2024.

technology.quote: low capacitance, low energy threshold, excellent energy resolution, single readout channel (in its simplest version), low cost, robustness, and flexibility in gas choice and operating pressure
technology.value: Spherical proportional counter (SPC): a large gas-filled copper sphere with a single small sensor electrode at the centre, sensitive to single ionization electrons
